Organic phosphates, phosphothioates, and phosphodithioates are commonly found in pesticides and insecticides. When these compounds are mixed with caustics (strong bases like sodium hydroxide or potassium hydroxide), they undergo alkaline hydrolysis.

The main hazard in this reaction is that these organophosphorus compounds can decompose under alkaline conditions to release toxic gases. Specifically, phosphothioates and phosphodithioates contain sulfur atoms that can be released as hydrogen sulfide (H₂S) gas during decomposition, which is highly toxic. Additionally, other toxic phosphorus-containing gases may be generated.
